source_acquisition.search_note: PDF p.1 explicitly links the selected repository, whose README description/title exactly matches the paper. Read-only gh repo view, recursive tree, and code searches confirmed implementation files but no plot*, figure*, visual*, table*, LaTeX/TikZ/PGF, SVG, notebook, style, or plotting script; exact-title repository search returned only this repository. Dao-AILab/flash-attention and karpathy/nanoGPT are cited ecosystem candidates, not validated visual sources. Figure 10 is an issue screenshot and has no author-owned editable visual source.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Local blue/red line grammars serve failure, mechanism, and stabilization curves; red/blue diverging maps serve matrices; blue/orange lines distinguish Llama tokens; a blue-to-yellow sequential map serves spectral norms; and the token grid uses a multi-colour diverging scale. No global colour dictionary exists and hue carries several important distinctions.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Most axes, heatmap cells, labels, and plotted lines are vector PDF content. Figure 1 contains small embedded raster/icon objects; Figure 10 contains two embedded raster screenshots; indexed raster colour-bar strips appear beside several otherwise vector-like maps. The document is mixed rather than uniformly vector.
paper_style.style_consistency: Captions and body equations consistently use Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern, while plotted labels mix Arial/DejaVu Sans and Figure 1/10 imported office or screenshot fonts. Main plots share a compact grid/blue-red grammar; appendix matrices and screenshots are denser and less unified.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Analysis in different sections. Our paper traces the causal chain of training failure (blue box) in reverse to identify the root causes.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue marks the traced/selected chain and section tabs; pale blue encloses the causal panel; green marks claims/positive terms; red/orange emphasize error or endpoint; black and white carry text and boxes.

encodings.color: causal-panel, section, claim, and endpoint emphasis
encodings.shape: section cards, rounded boxes, and arrows
encodings.facet: left section navigation versus right root-cause chain
encodings.text: section names, claims, formulas, and the loss-explosion endpoint

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual synthesis rather than a sampled estimate. It compresses δ/O localization → common low-rank R and positive bias → spectral-norm growth → loss explosion, then places dynamic maximum as the mitigation. No sample size, uncertainty, aggregation, or fitted statistic is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Connects §3.2 Claim 1, §3.3.1 Claim 2, §3.3.2 Claim 3, and §4. Figures 2–6 instantiate failure/localization/mechanism and Figure 7 instantiates the intervention; Algorithms 1–3 supply implementation details.
design_strengths: Makes the long causal chain scannable before the equations.
Binds section numbers, claims, mechanism terms, and intervention into one navigational object.
design_weaknesses: Equation, arrows, claim text, and endpoint compete in a small canvas.
Mixed imported typography and hue-dependent emphasis are fragile under grayscale or downscaling.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a reverse causal map to connect a high-level failure, local arithmetic boundary, mechanism decomposition, and minimal intervention before dense quantitative panels.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: The failure case using BF16 and flash attention results in a sudden loss explosion, while the stable configuration converges.

color.semantic_mapping: High-precision and low-precision configurations are separated by blue/red trajectory color; the neutral gray role is the grid/background.

encodings.color: precision configuration: high precision versus low precision
encodings.shape: small point markers on the trajectories
encodings.text: axis labels, title, and precision legend

figures.data_and_statistics: One fixed failure replay, not a seed-level aggregate. The low-precision curve falls toward roughly 3–4 and jumps near 7,000 steps to about 7–8; the high-precision curve continues to converge. No uncertainty, denominator, repeated runs, or formal failure threshold is displayed.
figures.evidence_relation: First empirical object after Figure 1: establishes the failure node that §3.2 diagnoses through tiling, layer, and precision substitutions. Appendix Figure 10 provides community context rather than a matched replication.
design_strengths: Immediate failure/stability contrast with one metric and step axis.
The jump is visually unmistakable.
design_weaknesses: Inset labels and caption color mapping are small.
One replay cannot communicate occurrence frequency or variability; explosion is a visual decision rather than a quantified threshold.
figures.reusable_pattern: Open a numerical-instability paper with a matched failure/control trajectory, then reuse the axis vocabulary for intervention plots.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: W^Q of attention head 8 has the largest spectral norm. Subsequent analysis focuses on this head.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue line/markers encode head-wise spectral norm and gray carries the grid.

encodings.color: single blue data series against neutral grid
encodings.shape: point markers, with numeric values printed near points
encodings.text: direct values, head names, and axis labels

figures.data_and_statistics: A single layer-1 head-wise snapshot used to choose head 8 (about 6.27) for downstream analysis. Values are displayed without seed aggregation, uncertainty, normalization, or inferential comparison.
figures.evidence_relation: Operationalizes the spectral-alignment probe and determines the head used in Figures 4–6. Figure 11 later broadens the spectral-norm view across layers and training steps.
design_strengths: Direct numeric labels make the selected head auditable.
Compact categorical line is easy to scan.
design_weaknesses: Direct labels and rotated head names are tiny.
No error/replication information or complete selection protocol; a connected line may imply continuity between categorical heads.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a directly labeled screening plot to justify which module/head receives the expensive mechanism analysis, then show the broader map in an appendix.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: PK, X, and (PK)[T ]^T X[T ] at different batch indices and training steps. (c) and (f) show that (PK)[T ]^T X[T ] for different tokens and training steps have some similar columns in input features 546 and 678.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/red encode signed matrix values and white/gray the neutral background; the structure of similar columns is read mainly through the diverging hue pattern.

encodings.facet: two batch/training settings × PK, X, and rank-1 outer-product panels
encodings.text: panel titles, indices, and panel letters

figures.data_and_statistics: Selected slices: batch 190/training 6610/token 50 and batch 209/training 6619/token 718. The evidence is visual structural alignment; no rank estimate, cosine distribution, similarity threshold, uncertainty, or across-slice aggregation is plotted.
figures.evidence_relation: Visual bridge from Eq. (2) rank-1 terms to the common R approximation in Eq. (3) and Claim 2. It precedes Figure 5 coefficient accumulation and Figure 11 global spectral context.
design_strengths: Repeated geometry and color bars enable comparison of PK, X, and the derived outer products.
Panel titles preserve selected batch/step provenance.
design_weaknesses: Six dense maps and tiny ticks are difficult to quantify.
Separate color bars complicate cross-panel comparison; similar columns are asserted visually rather than summarized by a reproducible metric.
figures.reusable_pattern: Place source matrices and the derived rank-1 object in a consistent grid, with repeated conditions in rows, when explaining a mechanistic decomposition.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5: Analysis of δ = rowsum(dO ◦ O).

color.semantic_mapping: Blue encodes O-like quantities, red encodes dO/output error, gray is grid, and white is the background. Color distinguishes paired variables and the dual axes.

encodings.y: cumulative δ difference, O/dO, or output error/dO; panels (b–c) use paired linear y scales
encodings.color: blue/red variable identity and axis pairing
encodings.text: panel labels, variable names, feature positions, and local legends

figures.data_and_statistics: One replay and selected token T=718. Panel (a) follows cumulative (δ_lp−δ_hp)[T] over iterations 6580–6680; panels (b–c) emphasize features 20 and 29. No intervals, repeated trajectories, or full-token aggregation are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Turns Claim 2’s scalar coefficient into a local sign-alignment check: positive cumulative δ difference, then dO and output-error signs that make the product positive. Figure 6 continues from the output-error panel to P̄V arithmetic.
design_strengths: Three panels keep accumulation, gradient magnitude, and error sign together.
Dual axes reveal the tiny gradient/error scale beside the larger output signal.
design_weaknesses: Dual axes and color-only variable identity impose reading burden.
Short caption leaves panel semantics to prose; selected token/features limit generality.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a cumulative panel plus aligned local sign panels to connect a scalar mechanism coefficient to the upstream/downstream quantities that generate it.

figures.label: Figure 6

color.semantic_mapping: Blue encodes P̄, red encodes V/error, gray is grid, and white is background. Hue separates the two y-axis quantities.

encodings.y: P̄, V, or cumulative output error on paired linear y scales
encodings.color: P̄ versus V/error variable and second axis
encodings.line: full-token, cumulative-error, and zoomed error trajectories
encodings.facet: full-token context, cumulative error, and detail view
encodings.text: feature/variable names, axes, legends, and panel letters

figures.data_and_statistics: Selected T=718 and feature i=20. Panel (a) shows mostly negative V[:,i]; panels (b–c) show negative error jumps where P̄[T,i]=1. No event-frequency distribution or uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Follows Figure 5’s sign correlation and supports Eq. (4)–(5), Claim 3, and the bit-level arithmetic example on pages 8–9. It is the last main-body diagnostic before Figure 7.
design_strengths: Full-token and zoomed panels make the jump location concrete.
Paired P̄/error traces preserve the proposed arithmetic ordering.
design_weaknesses: Dual axes and tiny tick labels make magnitude comparisons fragile.
Color-only variable identity is not robust in grayscale; one token/feature slice cannot establish event frequency.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a global event trace with a zoomed local panel, keeping the trigger variable and accumulated error visually aligned.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7: Validation losses for classical flash attention and the stablized flash attention with AdamW, Muon optimizers, and GPT-2M model.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue is stabilized FA, red is classical FA, and gray is grid. The two series are separated almost entirely by hue.

encodings.x: training steps on a log scale
encodings.y: validation loss on a log scale
encodings.line: two loss trajectories; red termination/vertical growth encodes failure
encodings.text: configuration titles, log-scale labels, legends, and panel letters

figures.data_and_statistics: Three deterministic training curves: GPT-2S/AdamW and GPT-2S/Muon are described to 600K steps and GPT-2M/AdamW to 100K. Stabilized FA uses β=2 and classical FA explodes. No seed aggregation, confidence bands, final-loss table, or runtime/memory overhead is present.
figures.evidence_relation: Main-body validation of the dynamic-maximum intervention in §4 and Algorithm 3. It closes the chain from Figures 2–6 to a practical mitigation; Appendix C/E gives conditional behavior and pseudocode.
design_strengths: Common log-axis small multiples make the intervention comparison easy to scan.
Early convergence and late explosion remain visible in one grammar.
design_weaknesses: Color is the only method discriminator.
Truncated exploding curves and different budgets complicate cross-panel magnitude comparison; no uncertainty or cost object accompanies “minimal”.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched small multiples for a numerical intervention across optimizer/model stress points, retaining common log axes and a fixed control color.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8: Similar (PK)[T ]^T X[T ] discovered at different tokens in Llama-3.1-8B. (c)-(f) show the similar columns.

color.semantic_mapping: Heatmap blue/white/red encodes matrix magnitude; blue/orange lines distinguish token 3/4; gray is grid. Token identity is also written in titles/legends.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: upper right for line panels; right-side color bars for heatmaps

encodings.x: hidden/head dimensions in heatmaps and head dimension in lower line charts
encodings.color: heatmap magnitude and blue/orange token identity
encodings.shape: rectangular heatmap cells or line markers
encodings.facet: two token heatmaps and four selected-column line groups

figures.data_and_statistics: One Llama-3.1-8B layer-1/head-13 sentence example (“The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog”), selected columns, and cosine similarities around 0.999994/0.999993. This is a qualitative structural observation with no Llama training outcome, uncertainty, or population distribution.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix D extends the common-R observation beyond GPT-2 while explicitly limiting the claim: the paper states that the Llama pattern does not imply Llama will definitely fail in BF16 training. It supports structural robustness, not failure generalization.
design_strengths: Repeated heatmap/line pairing makes selected columns inspectable.
Cosine similarity and model/token context remain visible in panel titles.
design_weaknesses: Ten axes in a page-width object are very small.
Mixed scales prevent direct cross-panel reading; selected columns and one sentence are not a systematic cross-model test.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a global representation map with per-column traces and an explicit similarity value when transporting a mechanism observation without overclaiming failure generality.

figures.label: Figure 9

caption.text: Figure 9: Two maxima observed in Llama-3.1-8B. The first token has maxima due to the attention sink.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue point marks encode attention probability; gray is the grid and no color comparison is carried.

encodings.text: direct layer/head/query titles and panel letters

figures.data_and_statistics: Six selected Llama queries show a first-token attention-sink maximum and another high maximum at a later key position, with most other points near zero. No frequency estimate, uncertainty, or prevalence threshold is given.
figures.evidence_relation: Supports Appendix D.2’s multiple-maxima premise that motivates the P̄=1 arithmetic mechanism, but is not an author-run Llama failure experiment. Figure 13 returns to GPT-2 for temporal activation/loss alignment.
design_strengths: Common axes make the repeated two-maxima pattern comparable.
Direct titles preserve layer/head/query provenance.
design_weaknesses: Dense near-zero points collapse into a band.
Six hand-selected examples cannot quantify prevalence; “two maxima” may read broader than the shown queries.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use same-scale small multiples to show a recurrent attention pattern across selected contexts, with model scope explicit.

figures.label: Figure 10

caption.text: Figure 10: Loss curves of two independent runs of GPT-2 training with flash attention in BF16 reported in the Github issue of nanoGPT.

color.semantic_mapping: Panel (a) uses a blue loss line on a light screenshot; panel (b) uses magenta/orange run lines on a dark screenshot; white carries background/text in the light panel.

encodings.line: loss traces as preserved in issue screenshots
encodings.text: screenshot UI titles, panel captions, and issue labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Two community-reported runs, not a controlled author-run aggregate. Panel (a) has a short step range; panel (b) shows two trajectories through roughly 130k iterations. No raw data, dates, seeds, uncertainty, or harmonized y-scale are supplied.
figures.evidence_relation: Provides independent failure context referenced by §3.1 and complements author Figure 2; it is background/reproduction evidence rather than a replacement for the fixed replay or causal substitutions.
design_strengths: Preserves community provenance and more than one observed failure report.
Stacked screenshots retain the original visual evidence.
design_weaknesses: Raster text and dark/light backgrounds conflict with main-plot style.
Scales and UI labels differ; only issue numbers identify provenance and no editable visual source is linked.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use clearly labeled external screenshots only as contextual failure evidence, separate from controlled experiments.

figures.label: Figure 11

caption.text: Figure 11: Spectral norm across layers and training steps.

color.semantic_mapping: Dark blue is low spectral norm and yellow is high spectral norm; the color bar is labeled Spectral Norm Value.

encodings.text: long row names, ticks, title, and color-bar label

figures.data_and_statistics: Longitudinal heatmap over the GPT-2 replay, with approximately 72 rows (six attention/MLP weight groups × 12 layers) and sampled training steps. It shows an outlier band rather than a distribution, uncertainty, denominator, or cross-run statistic.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix expansion of spectral-norm localization in §3.2, connected to Figures 3–5; supplies global context for selecting the exceptional attention module/head.
design_strengths: One dense layer-by-time view exposes the abnormal band and timing.
Row labels preserve parameter-group identity.
design_weaknesses: Long labels and tiny cells are difficult to read.
Sequential hue is printer-dependent and no numeric table or uncertainty accompanies the outlier.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a layer-by-time heatmap to triage where instability emerges, then pair it with a direct-label screening plot.

figures.label: Figure 12

color.semantic_mapping: D_diff magnitude/sign is encoded by a blue-to-red diverging scale; neutral cells/borders are gray/white and token identity is written in cells.

encodings.text: token strings, sum annotation, and D_diff color-bar label

figures.data_and_statistics: Dense token-level difference visualization with a visible “Sum: 1.81e-06” annotation, but no readable axis units, sample denominator, aggregation definition, or uncertainty. The PDF text extractor emits unrelated/fragmented token strings; the rendered grid and caption are the only reliable visual semantics.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix-only diagnostic not called by the central visual chain; it sits beside Figure 13 and additional details and does not carry the central failure or mitigation decision.
design_strengths: Direct token labels and color bar make local-difference inspection apparent.
Warm outlier cells are easy to locate.
design_weaknesses: Cell text and color differences are too small for reliable reading.
Caption omits axis/definition information and extraction corruption makes this the least auditable figure.
figures.reusable_pattern: For token-level diagnostics, pair a cell grid with direct token labels and an explicit diverging scale, and define the difference and axes in the caption/header.

figures.label: Figure 13

caption.text: Figure 13: Correlation between multiple maxima occurrences and loss curve.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue is validation loss, red is activated SFA-condition count, and gray is grid; separate left/right axis labels redundantly state the variable identity.

encodings.y: validation loss on the left and activated SFA-condition count on the right (both linear)
encodings.color: loss versus condition-count series and matching axis labels
encodings.text: title, dual axis labels, multiplier, legend, and training-step ticks

figures.data_and_statistics: One trajectory from approximately 0–14,000 steps. The activated-condition count rises around 7,000–10,000 steps before/alongside the loss jump; no lag estimate, predictive threshold, repeated runs, or uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Visualizes Appendix E.1’s leading-indicator suggestion and complements Figure 2; it is not an independent mitigation result and does not replace Figure 7’s matched curves.
design_strengths: Shared x-axis makes temporal ordering visible.
Dual axes preserve each quantity’s native scale.
design_weaknesses: Dual-axis overlay can imply calibrated correlation without lag/statistical analysis.
Single-run timing is insufficient for prediction; hue dependence weakens print robustness.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a dual-axis time trace only with a clearly labeled time base, and pair visual lead/lag with an explicit lag or prediction metric.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 gives the reverse causal map; Figure 2 establishes failure; Figure 3 chooses the exceptional head; Figure 4 visualizes the shared low-rank direction; Figure 5 links δ accumulation to signs; Figure 6 localizes the P̄V rounding event; Figure 7 tests dynamic maximum. Figures 8–13 extend structural, community, longitudinal, token, and temporal context in the appendix.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use the serif body font and Figure n: prefix. Figures 1–4 and 7 include setup/comparison or a finding, while Figures 5, 6, 11, and 12 are terse labels. Figures 8–10 and 13 provide partial scope but leave scales or selections to panel titles/prose; no caption uses a bold conclusion header.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: No tables or table headers are physically present. Quantitative variable definitions are carried by plot axes, legends, colour bars, and nearby prose.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Algorithms 1–3 and equations define the arithmetic boundary; Figures 2–6 provide failure/localization/mechanism evidence; Figure 7 provides the intervention comparison. The link is strong in the main paper, but precision substitutions and targeted outcomes are not consolidated in a table.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Appendix D Figures 8–9 broaden structural/multiple-maxima observations with an explicit Llama scope limit; Figure 10 documents community context; Figure 11 expands spectral tracking; Figures 12–13 add diagnostics. Algorithms 1–3 and Appendices B/C/E provide implementation/proof context. Figure 13 is called from E.1; Figure 12 is largely uncited by the main storyline.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Captions/body equations are consistent Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern, but plotted labels mix Arial/DejaVu Sans and imported office/screenshot fonts. Main figures are readable at rendered size; appendix matrices and screenshots are substantially denser.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/red is reused for precision, O/dO, classical/stabilized FA, and loss/count, but semantic assignment changes by figure. Diverging maps and sequential spectral maps use local bars; no shared palette legend or redundant line-style convention exists.

most_reusable_patterns: Reverse-map a long numerical mechanism into failure, localization, root cause, and intervention nodes (Figure 1).
Use a fixed replay and precision/module substitutions before causal interpretation (Figures 2–3 and surrounding text).
Pair source matrices with derived rank-1 maps, cumulative coefficients, local sign traces, and a zoomed arithmetic event (Figures 4–6).
Validate a minimal intervention with common axes across optimizer/model small multiples (Figure 7), while placing implementation edge cases in appendix algorithms.
highest_value_objects: Figure 5 for connecting δ to gradient/output signs.
Figure 7 for the practical stabilization decision.
failure_patterns: Very short or non-self-contained captions for Figures 5, 6, 11, and 12.
Color-only variable identity and dual y-axes without scale/lag guidance.
Selected single trajectories/slices presented without uncertainty or population context.
Appendix heatmaps and token grids with labels too small for reliable reading.
Screenshots with inconsistent UI, scales, and typography.
No visual cost/overhead object for the minimal intervention claim.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a reverse causal map plus progressively local diagnostics—from replayed loss failure through low-rank/sign/rounding evidence to a common-axis stabilization test—while moving dense cross-model and token-level context to an appendix without editable plotting sources.
